nodes.label: New Media
nodes.description: The overarching subject of the book, defined by digital medium's material and logical organization.

nodes.label: Numerical Representation
nodes.description: First principle of new media: all new media objects are composed of digital code.

nodes.label: Modularity
nodes.description: Second principle of new media: fractal structure of new media objects.

nodes.label: Automation
nodes.description: Third principle of new media: removal of human intentionality from the creative process.

nodes.label: Variability
nodes.description: Fourth principle of new media: a new media object can exist in different, potentially infinite versions.

nodes.label: Transcoding
nodes.description: Fifth principle of new media: translating something into another format, combining computer and cultural layers.

nodes.label: The Interface
nodes.description: The human-computer interface, shaped by traditions of print, cinema, and HCI.

nodes.label: The Operations
nodes.description: Software applications which run on top of the OS, their interfaces and typical operations like compositing and teleaction.

nodes.label: The Illusions
nodes.description: Appearance, and the new logic of digital images created and accessed using software applications.

nodes.label: The Forms
nodes.description: The commonly used conventions for organizing a new media object as a whole, such as Database and Navigable space.

nodes.label: Cinema
nodes.description: A key cultural form of the twentieth century that serves as the conceptual lens to look at new media.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.description: A new media form representing the logic of organizing information, often contrasted with narrative.

nodes.label: Navigable Space
nodes.description: A new media form centered on movement through a simulated 3D space.

nodes.label: Dziga Vertov's A Man With a Movie Camera
nodes.description: An early avant-garde film serving as a visual index and precursor to the language of new media and database imagination.
